intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from legendary vendors. Engage with local chefs and discover the heart of Tokyo's food culture in one of the world's most famous market districts.

experiences.name: Akihabara Electric Town Tech Immersion
experiences.description: Dive deep into Tokyo's iconic tech and otaku hub. Browse multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera, visit retro gaming arcades, explore robot and AI gadget shops, and experience maid cafes. A must-do for anyone fascinated by Japan's cutting-edge and pop tech culture.

experiences.name: Ramen Alley Crawl in Shinjuku
experiences.description: Navigate the narrow, atmospheric lanes of Shinjuku's Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) and nearby ramen shops to taste regional ramen styles — from rich tonkotsu to delicate shio broth. Chat with local chefs and experience the authentic izakaya dining culture under glowing lanterns.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in a world-renowned digital art experience created by the art collective teamLab. Walk through stunning interactive installations that blend technology, nature, and art in a borderless, ever-changing environment. A perfect fusion of Tokyo's tech innovation and cultural creativity.

experiences.name: Depachika Gourmet Basement Food Hall Experience
experiences.description: Descend into the legendary basement food halls (depachika) of Isetan or Takashimaya department stores. Sample artisan wagashi sweets, premium bento boxes, handcrafted chocolates, and regional Japanese delicacies. A uniquely Japanese culinary ritual that showcases the country's obsession with food quality and presentation.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Narita or Haneda Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly airport limousine bus or train to Tsukiji area (approx. 60-90 min). Check in to your Boutique Stay in Tsukiji, Chuo City. Drop off luggage and freshen up. Take a short orientation walk around the Tsukiji Outer Market neighborhood to get your bearings — browse the narrow lanes, fish monger stalls, and street food vendors still open in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Tsukiji Outer Market for your first Tokyo dinner. Explore the evening stalls and small eateries lining Shin-Ohashi-dori. Try a bowl of fresh seafood donburi or grilled scallops on a stick from street vendors. End the night with a short walk along the Sumida River waterfront to enjoy the city lights and decompress from travel.

meals.breakfast: N/A (in transit)
meals.lunch: Grab a convenience store bento or onigiri at 7-Eleven or Lawson near the airport or train station (¥300–¥600) — a quintessential budget Tokyo experience
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market street food: grilled seafood skewers, tamagoyaki (egg omelet), and a seafood rice bowl from one of the market stalls (¥800–¥1,500 total)

day_by_day.notes: Get a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport — it works on all trains, subways, and buses and saves money vs. buying individual tickets. Jet lag tip: stay awake until at least 21:00 local time to adjust faster. Tsukiji Outer Market stalls begin closing around 14:00–15:00, but many restaurants and smaller shops stay open into the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (6:00–7:00) to experience Tsukiji Outer Market at its most vibrant. Browse the fresh seafood, pickles, tea, and kitchenware stalls. Grab a legendary Tsukiji breakfast: fresh sushi or a seafood rice bowl from one of the iconic breakfast spots like Sushi Dai or Daiwa Sushi (arrive early — lines form fast). Explore the surrounding Tsukiji Honganji Temple, a stunning Buddhist temple with free entry just minutes from the market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short subway ride to Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 entry — one of Tokyo's best budget garden experiences). Stroll through the traditional Japanese landscape garden with a tidal pond, seasonal flowers, and views of modern skyscrapers as a backdrop. Cross the Sumida River by the garden's ferry boat (¥200–¥350) to Asakusa for a classic old-Tokyo afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Asakusa's Nakamise Shopping Street and Senso-ji Temple (free entry, open 24 hours). Browse affordable souvenir shops and snack stalls along the approach. Wander the backstreets of Hoppy Street for cheap yakitori and draft beer. Take the Tokyo Skytree observation deck if budget allows (¥2,100 for lower deck) or simply admire it lit up from the ground for free.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast sushi set or seafood donburi at a market stall (¥1,000–¥1,800)
meals.lunch: Grab a cheap lunch set (teishoku) at a local soba or ramen shop near Hamarikyu or Asakusa (¥700–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Hoppy Street in Asakusa: yakitori skewers, motsuni (offal stew), and Hoppy beer — a beloved budget Tokyo drinking and dining tradition (¥1,000–¥1,800 total)

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is most lively 6:00–10:00. The inner wholesale market has relocated to Toyosu but the outer market remains a foodie paradise. Hamarikyu Gardens is closed on Mondays. Senso-ji Temple is free and especially atmospheric at night.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Akihabara — Tokyo's legendary Electric Town and the heart of tech and otaku culture. Spend the morning exploring multi-floor electronics shops like Yodobashi Camera and Sofmap, retro game shops, and component stores along Chuo-dori. Browse the latest gadgets, vintage Famicom cartridges, DIY electronics kits at Radio Kaikan, and tech curiosities. Window shopping is free and endlessly fascinating.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue deeper into Akihabara's side streets to find smaller doujinshi shops, figure stores, and maid cafes (budget option: just peek inside or opt for a ¥500–¥700 entry maid cafe). Visit the free floors of Yodobashi Akiba to see Japan's cutting-edge consumer tech. Then head to the nearby 3331 Arts Chiyoda (free entry to most areas) — a repurposed school turned arts and tech innovation space.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Kanda Myojin Shrine (free, open late) — a historic shrine popular with tech workers and IT companies who come to pray for digital protection and cybersecurity. Then explore the izakayas and ramen shops in the Kanda and Ochanomizu area for a budget dinner. Return to Tsukiji via subway.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near your hotel: onigiri, tamagoyaki, and canned coffee from 7-Eleven or FamilyMart (¥300–¥500)
meals.lunch: Akihabara curry: try one of the many Japanese curry chain restaurants like CoCo Ichibanya or a local curry shop — filling and budget-friendly (¥700–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Ramen at a local shop in Kanda or Akihabara area — try Ichiran or a local independent ramen-ya for a bowl under ¥1,000. Add a gyoza side for ¥300

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on foot — the main strip is Chuo-dori but the real gems are in the side alleys. Many electronics shops have tax-free shopping for tourists (bring your passport). Maid cafes are a cultural experience unique to Akihabara — even a short visit gives insight into otaku culture.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Shibuya for a morning exploring one of Tokyo's most iconic districts. Start at the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing — arrive by 9:00 for a less crowded but still impressive experience. Visit the free Shibuya Sky observation deck alternative: the rooftop of Shibuya Hikarie (lower floors free, great views). Walk up the hill to Daikanyama, a trendy but low-key neighborhood with independent bookshops and cafes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shimokitazawa by train from Shibuya (2 stops, ¥160) — Tokyo's beloved bohemian neighborhood packed with vintage clothing stores, indie record shops, small live music venues, and quirky cafes. This is a paradise for tech-culture-adjacent creative subcultures. Browse secondhand shops for unique finds. The area is very walkable and the street food is cheap.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Shibuya for the evening rush — the scramble crossing is most dramatic at dusk and after dark. Grab dinner in the basement food hall (depachika) of Shibuya Hikarie or Tokyu Food Show for high-quality affordable prepared foods and bento. Walk through the neon-lit streets of Shibuya's entertainment district and people-watch.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local kissaten (old-school Japanese coffee shop) in Tsukiji or Shibuya — morning set (toast, egg, coffee) for ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Shimokitazawa: grab a cheap curry, falafel wrap, or sandwich from one of the many independent eateries (¥600–¥900)
meals.dinner: Shibuya depachika (department store basement food hall) — pick up sushi, prepared dishes, and discounted bento (especially good after 19:00 when stores discount remaining stock) for ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means Shibuya and Shimokitazawa are busier but more lively. Shimokitazawa's vintage shops and music venues are a window into Tokyo's indie subculture — very different from Akihabara but equally fascinating. Depachika discount shopping after 19:00 is a classic Tokyo budget hack.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Harajuku. Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine (free entry) in the morning — a serene forested Shinto shrine in the middle of the city, especially peaceful on Sunday mornings. Walk through the towering torii gate and forested path. Then stroll down Takeshita Street for Tokyo's most colorful street fashion, crepe stands, and pop culture shops — all very affordable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Harajuku through Omotesando — Tokyo's tree-lined 'Champs-Élysées' — to Aoyama. Browse the architecture and window-shop the flagship stores (free to look). Visit the Nezu Museum garden (¥1,300) for a peaceful traditional Japanese garden experience, or opt for the free Omotesando Hills exterior and street architecture tour. Head to the nearby Spiral Building in Aoyama for free contemporary art and design exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Tsukiji/Ginza area. Explore Ginza on a Sunday evening when Chuo-dori is closed to traffic (pedestrian paradise until 17:00 in warmer months). Window shop the luxury district for free and enjoy the atmosphere. Grab dinner at a nearby affordable restaurant in the less touristy backstreets between Ginza and Tsukiji.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku crepe from one of the iconic Takeshita Street crepe stands — a sweet Tokyo staple (¥500–¥700)
meals.lunch: Harajuku or Omotesando: try a budget Japanese lunch set at a local teishoku restaurant or grab a bento from a convenience store in the area (¥600–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji-area izakaya near your hotel — look for set course menus or happy hour deals at local spots (¥1,000–¥1,500 with a drink)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free but a small donation at the main hall is customary. Sunday morning is the best time to visit — serene and less crowded. Takeshita Street opens around 10:00–11:00. Ginza's pedestrian Sunday closure (hokoten) typically runs April through November, 12:00–17:00.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Odaiba, Tokyo's futuristic artificial island in Tokyo Bay — a must for tech culture enthusiasts. Take the driverless Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi (scenic and fun, ¥330 one way) for a great view of Rainbow Bridge and the bay. Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets (tickets ¥3,200 — worth it for the immersive digital art experience). Book in advance online to save time.
day_by_day.afternoon: After teamLab, explore the rest of Odaiba for free: the life-size Unicorn Gundam statue at DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (free to view), the retro arcade games at Joypolis (free to enter, pay per game), and the waterfront promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline. Visit the Toyota Mega Web showroom (free) to see concept cars and future mobility technology.
day_by_day.evening: Take the water bus (Suijo Bus) from Odaiba back to Hinode Pier near Hamamatsucho (¥480–¥780) for a scenic Tokyo Bay cruise at dusk. Walk back toward Tsukiji or take a short subway ride. Enjoy dinner at a local neighborhood restaurant near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near Shimbashi station before boarding the Yurikamome (¥300–¥500)
meals.lunch: Odaiba: grab a meal at the Aqua City Odaiba food court — multiple affordable options including ramen, sushi, and Japanese fast food (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Local neighborhood izakaya near Tsukiji hotel — order the daily special (higawari teishoku) for a complete meal with rice, miso soup, and a main dish (¥800–¥1,200)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets sell out — book at least 2–3 days in advance at teamlab.art. The Yurikamome monorail ride itself is a highlight with panoramic bay views. Toyota Mega Web is free and genuinely impressive for tech enthusiasts. The water bus back is a scenic and affordable alternative to the monorail.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Shinjuku. Start at the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (open from 9:00, free) on the 45th floor — one of the best free panoramic views of Tokyo, including Mount Fuji on clear days. Explore the surrounding Nishi-Shinjuku skyscraper district, which is a fascinating example of Japan's architectural ambition and urban planning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross to Higashi-Shinjuku (East Shinjuku). Visit the free Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry — worth it in April for late cherry blossoms or spring greenery). Stroll through the massive traditional Japanese, French formal, and English landscape gardens. Then explore Kabukicho, Tokyo's famous entertainment district, in the late afternoon — safe to walk around and fascinating to observe even without spending money.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — a tiny alley of tiny yakitori restaurants near Shinjuku Station West Exit. This is one of Tokyo's most atmospheric and affordable dining spots: grab a stool at a tiny grill counter, order skewers of chicken and vegetables, and drink cold beer surrounded by smoke and old Tokyo charm. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,000 for a full meal with drinks.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a Shinjuku convenience store or a standing soba shop (tachigui soba) near Shinjuku Station — fast, cheap, and delicious (¥350–¥600)
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen picnic-style: buy prepared foods from a nearby convenience store or supermarket and eat in the garden (total ¥500–¥800)
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori alley: chicken skewers, negima, tsukune, and cold draft beer at a tiny counter grill (¥1,500–¥2,000 including drinks)

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building has two observation towers — North Tower is generally open daily, South Tower has different hours. Check the official website. Shinjuku Gyoen is closed on Mondays. Omoide Yokocho is cash-only at most stalls — bring small bills. It gets very smoky inside — embrace the atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Koenji neighborhood — Tokyo's indie alternative culture hub. Take the JR Chuo Line from Shinjuku to Koenji (¥165). Browse the incredible density of vintage clothing shops, used record stores, and secondhand bookshops along the covered shopping arcades (shotengai). Koenji is beloved by musicians, artists, and Tokyo's creative underground — a fascinating contrast to the tech districts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the train to Nakameguro. Walk along the Meguro River canal — one of Tokyo's most scenic urban walks, especially beautiful with spring greenery overhanging the water. Browse the independent boutiques, cafes, and design shops lining the canal. Then head to Daikanyama T-Site — a stunning architectural bookshop and cultural complex (free to browse) that is itself a landmark of Japanese design culture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ebisu or Meguro for dinner. Explore the local izakayas and ramen shops in these less touristy residential neighborhoods for authentic and affordable Tokyo dining. Take the train back to Tsukiji via Hibiya or Hanzomon Line.

meals.breakfast: Local kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) in Tsukiji or Koenji — morning set with toast, egg, and coffee (¥400–¥700)
meals.lunch: Koenji: try a local curry shop, ramen-ya, or teishoku restaurant in the covered shopping arcade — filling lunch for ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Meguro or Ebisu neighborhood izakaya — order a mix of small dishes (tsukidashi appetizer, sashimi, grilled fish, and vegetables) with one drink for ¥1,200–¥1,800

day_by_day.notes: Koenji is best explored on foot — the vintage shops are concentrated around the north and south exits of Koenji Station. Nakameguro is most famous for cherry blossoms in late March/early April — by mid-April the blossoms may be fading but the canal walk remains beautiful with green leaves. Daikanyama T-Site is open until 26:00 (2:00 AM) — one of Tokyo's most architecturally significant bookshops.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ueno — one of Tokyo's great cultural and park districts. Ueno Park (free entry) is home to multiple world-class museums and a large public park. Explore the park's paths, Shinobazu Pond with its lotus beds, and the free-entry Ueno Toshogu Shrine. Choose one museum to visit: the Tokyo National Museum (¥1,000) for Japan's finest collection of art and antiquities, or the National Museum of Nature and Science (¥630) for science and technology history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Ueno to the nearby Yanaka neighborhood — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) districts. Stroll through Yanaka Ginza shopping street, a charming traditional shotengai with cheap snacks, local shops, and a genuine neighborhood atmosphere. Explore the atmospheric Yanaka Cemetery (free, open to public) with its old trees and historic graves. Visit the small temples and shrines scattered throughout the area.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or take the train to Nezu or Sendagi for dinner in the quiet backstreets. Try a local tofu restaurant, soba shop, or family-run izakaya in this traditional neighborhood. Return to Tsukiji via Chiyoda Line from Nezu Station.

meals.breakfast: Ameyoko Market near Ueno Station: grab fresh fruit, grilled squid, or a quick snack from the open-air market stalls (¥300–¥600)
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza street food: try menchi katsu (fried meat croquette), korokke, or grilled fish from the shotengai stalls — a classic cheap Tokyo lunch (¥400–¥700)
meals.dinner: Yanaka/Nezu area: family-run soba restaurant or tofu kaiseki set — look for teishoku lunch sets still served in the early evening for extra savings (¥800–¥1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Ueno Park is free but most museums charge entry. Tuesday is the common closing day for many Tokyo museums — Thursday is generally safe. Yanaka is one of the few Tokyo neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing intact, giving it a rare old-Tokyo atmosphere. Ameyoko is a lively open-air market that has operated since the post-war black market era — fascinating history and great cheap snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Toyosu Market — the world's largest fish market and the relocated successor to the famous Tsukiji inner market. Take the Yurakucho Line to Shijo-mae Station (¥210). Book a free viewing gallery spot in advance (online reservation required) to watch the famous tuna auctions from the observation deck. Even without the auction, the market tour areas and seafood restaurants are fascinating for food culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Tsukiji area and spend the afternoon exploring the Ginza district on foot — Tokyo's most prestigious shopping and cultural district. Visit the free Ginza Six rooftop garden, browse the Itoya stationery flagship store (free to browse — a Tokyo institution), and explore the Ginza Sony Park (free interactive tech and culture space from Sony). Walk through the backstreets between Ginza and Shimbashi for a mix of upscale and everyday Tokyo life.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Tsukishima neighborhood (a short walk or subway ride from Tsukiji) — famous for monjayaki, Tokyo's local savory pancake specialty. Tsukishima's Monja Street is lined with restaurants serving this uniquely Tokyo dish. Cook your own monjayaki at the table for an interactive, affordable, and delicious dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Toyosu Market: have breakfast at one of the seafood restaurants inside the market building — fresh sushi or seafood don for breakfast is a Tokyo bucket-list experience (¥1,500–¥2,500 — splurge breakfast)
meals.lunch: Ginza area: grab a budget lunch at a standing sushi bar (kaiten sushi or tachinomi sushi) in the Ginza/Shimbashi backstreets (¥800–¥1,200)
meals.dinner: Tsukishima Monja Street: monjayaki set with multiple toppings, cooked tableside, with a soft drink (¥1,200–¥1,800 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Toyosu tuna auction viewing requires advance reservation through the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market website — book as early as possible as slots fill up months ahead. The market restaurant area is excellent even without the auction. Monjayaki is Tokyo's answer to Osaka's okonomiyaki — a must-try local specialty. Most monja restaurants on Tsukishima's Monja Street are very affordable and staff are used to helping tourists cook.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Ikebukuro — a major hub with a distinct character from Shinjuku and Shibuya. Visit the free observation deck at the Sunshine City complex (Sunshine 60 building) or the more affordable Sunshine City Aquarium. Explore the Animate flagship store (Japan's largest anime merchandise retailer) and the dense concentration of manga, anime, and gaming shops in the Otome Road area — a fascinating tech and pop culture ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the train to Sugamo — nicknamed 'Grandma's Harajuku' — a charming traditional shopping street (Jizo-dori) catering to older Tokyoites. It's a fascinating cultural contrast to the youth-oriented districts and offers excellent cheap traditional snacks, pickles, and local goods. Visit Koganji Temple (free) and browse the red underwear shops and traditional confectionery stores. Then head to nearby Komagome for the stunning Rikugien Garden (¥300) — one of Tokyo's finest traditional landscape gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo via Yamanote Line. Spend the evening in the Yurakucho area near Ginza — explore the atmospheric izakayas built under the train tracks (gaado-shita izakayas) near Yurakucho Station. These brick-arched drinking spots are affordable, atmospheric, and beloved by Tokyo salarymen.

meals.breakfast: Ikebukuro: breakfast at a local bakery or standing coffee shop near the station (¥300–¥600)
meals.lunch: Sugamo Jizo-dori: try traditional Japanese sweets (wagashi), salt-grilled fish, or a cheap teishoku at a local restaurant on the shopping street (¥600–¥900)
meals.dinner: Yurakucho gaado-shita izakaya: draft beer, yakitori, and izakaya small plates under the train tracks — one of Tokyo's most atmospheric budget dining experiences (¥1,200–¥2,000 with drinks)

day_by_day.notes: Ikebukuro's Sunshine City Aquarium is ¥2,400 — skip if on a tight budget and just explore the free shopping complex and streets. Sugamo is best on weekends when the street is most lively. Rikugien Garden is especially beautiful in April with spring greenery and occasional late-blooming weeping cherry trees. Yurakucho gaado-shita izakayas are cash-preferred — bring yen.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Jimbocho — Tokyo's legendary used bookshop district. Over 170 secondhand bookstores line the streets, many with outdoor bargain bins. Even without reading Japanese, the manga, vintage maps, woodblock prints, and art books are fascinating. Visit Isseido Booksellers and the cluster of shops along Yasukuni-dori. Browse the outdoor stalls for cheap vintage prints and maps as souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Jimbocho to Akihabara (about 20 minutes on foot) for a second, deeper dive into Tokyo's tech culture. This time focus on the smaller specialist shops: visit the retro video game shops on the upper floors of Radio Kaikan, explore the Akihabara UDX building's tech exhibitions (often free), and browse the DIY electronics component shops on the side streets — a window into Japan's maker culture and engineering tradition.
day_by_day.evening: Last major evening out — head to Shinjuku for a farewell dinner and evening walk. Revisit your favorite spots or try a new area: explore the Golden Gai district (a labyrinth of tiny bars, each fitting 5–10 people) for a drink in one of Tokyo's most unique nightlife settings. Cover charges are typically ¥500–¥1,000 per bar but the experience is unforgettable.

meals.breakfast: Local neighborhood bakery or convenience store near your Tsukiji hotel (¥300–¥500)
meals.lunch: Jimbocho: the area has many affordable curry restaurants — Jimbocho is famous for its curry culture alongside its bookshops. Try a local curry shop for a hearty lunch (¥700–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Shinjuku: pre-Golden Gai dinner at a nearby ramen shop or gyoza restaurant in the Kabukicho backstreets (¥700–¥1,000), then drinks in Golden Gai (¥500–¥1,500 depending on bars visited)

day_by_day.notes: Jimbocho curry culture is a genuine Tokyo phenomenon — the neighborhood has dozens of curry restaurants of all styles (Japanese, Indian, Sri Lankan). Golden Gai bars each have their own personality and clientele — some are welcoming to tourists, others prefer regulars. Look for bars with English signs or tourist-friendly notices. Most require a small cover charge (otoshi/charge) — ask before sitting down.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo. Wake up early for one last visit to Tsukiji Outer Market — this time take your time buying gifts and food souvenirs: dried seafood, nori (seaweed), Japanese pickles, dashi stock packets, and kitchen tools make excellent affordable gifts. Say goodbye to the neighborhood that has been your base for 13 days. Check out of your hotel (standard checkout 10:00–11:00) and store luggage at the hotel or at a coin locker at the nearest subway station.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your final free hours at a nearby attraction: walk to Hama-rikyu Gardens for a final peaceful garden visit, or take the subway to Ginza for last-minute shopping at the 100-yen shops (Daiso on Chuo-dori) and Don Quijote for affordable Japanese snacks, cosmetics, and gifts. Head to the airport with plenty of time — allow 90–120 minutes travel time from central Tokyo to Narita or 60–90 minutes to Haneda.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Grab one final convenience store meal or airport ramen at the airport for a last taste of Tokyo food culture before your flight.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — treat yourself to a fresh sushi breakfast or tamagoyaki sandwich one last time (¥800–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Ginza or Tsukiji area: quick lunch set at a local soba or udon shop, or a convenience store bento if pressed for time (¥500–¥900)
meals.dinner: Airport: grab a final convenience store meal or eat at one of the airport's affordable ramen or soba restaurants before your flight (¥800–¥1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Coin lockers are available at most major Tokyo train stations (¥300–¥700 per day depending on size) — useful for storing luggage on your last day. Don Quijote (Donki) in Ginza is open 24 hours and is excellent for last-minute souvenir shopping at low prices. Remember to withdraw any remaining cash from ATMs before leaving — 7-Eleven ATMs accept international cards reliably. Return or top up your Suica card at the airport — you can get a refund of remaining balance minus a ¥220 fee.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Tsukiji area. Check in to the boutique hotel and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a relaxed walk through the Tsukiji Outer Market (仲見世通り周辺). Browse the stalls selling fresh seafood snacks, tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), and pickles. Get oriented with the neighborhood and pick up any essentials at a nearby convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a local izakaya near Tsukiji. Try Tsukiji Sushisay or a nearby ramen shop for an easy first-night meal. Stroll along the Sumida River waterfront as the city lights come on. Early night to recover from jet lag.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Meal on the plane or quick airport bite at Narita/Haneda
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market area izakaya or sushi counter — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Do not overplan Day 1. Jet lag is real — prioritize rest. Pick up a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Tsukiji Outer Market for a classic Tokyo breakfast — fresh sushi, grilled scallops, and tamagoyaki from market stalls. This is one of Tokyo's most authentic food experiences. Arrive by 8:00 AM for the best atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara (Electric Town) via the Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line. Explore multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and Bic Camera, retro game shops, and anime merchandise stores. Visit the AKIBA Cultures Zone and check out independent tech gadget shops.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Akihabara — try a themed café (maid café experience for cultural curiosity) or a hearty Japanese curry at CoCo Ichibanya. Return to Tsukiji via metro.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market stalls — fresh sushi set or tamagoyaki sandwich, ¥800–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Akihabara ramen or tonkatsu restaurant — ¥1,000–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Japanese curry or izakaya in Akihabara — ¥1,500–¥2,500

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is a must for tech culture enthusiasts. Many shops open around 10:00–11:00 AM. Retro game shops on upper floors of buildings are often hidden gems.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hamarikyu Gardens (浜離宮恩賜庭園), a beautiful traditional Japanese garden just a 10-minute walk from the hotel. Enjoy seasonal spring flowers and the serene tidal pond. Entry fee is around ¥300.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Yurikamome Line to Odaiba, Tokyo's futuristic man-made island. Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets (book in advance online) — a world-renowned digital art museum that perfectly blends tech and art culture. Explore the surrounding waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Odaiba at DiverCity Tokyo Plaza food floor or a restaurant with a view of the Rainbow Bridge. Return to hotel via Yurikamome or water bus.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — ¥500–¥1,000
meals.lunch: Odaiba food court or ramen shop — ¥1,000–¥1,800
meals.dinner: DiverCity Tokyo or waterfront restaurant — ¥2,000–¥3,000

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab tickets well in advance — they sell out quickly, especially on weekends. The water bus from Hamarikyu to Odaiba is a scenic and fun option (¥480).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Asakusa (浅草). Visit Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest and most iconic temple. Explore Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional snacks, crafts, and souvenirs. Arrive early (before 9:00 AM) to avoid weekend crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Sumida River to the Tokyo Skytree (東京スカイツリー). Ascend to the observation deck for panoramic city views (¥2,100–¥3,100 depending on deck level). Explore the Solamachi shopping complex at the base.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner near Asakusa — try Sometaro (okonomiyaki restaurant) or a traditional tempura restaurant. Enjoy the evening atmosphere of old Tokyo (shitamachi culture).

meals.breakfast: Asakusa traditional snacks from Nakamise Street — ningyo-yaki, melonpan, ¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Solamachi food floor or soba restaurant near Skytree — ¥1,200–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Okonomiyaki or tempura in Asakusa — ¥1,800–¥2,800

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter. Skytree tickets can be purchased on-site or online. Asakusa to Tsukiji is easily accessible via the Toei Asakusa Line — very convenient from your hotel area.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ginza (銀座), Tokyo's upscale shopping and cultural district, a short walk or metro ride from Tsukiji. Explore the Sony Park and Itoya (a legendary 12-floor stationery and design store). Window shop the flagship luxury stores and admire the architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Panasonic Center Tokyo in Ariake or visit the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) on Odaiba — an excellent tech-focused museum with exhibits on robotics, AI, and space exploration. ASIMO robot demonstrations are highlights.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ginza for dinner. Try a mid-range sushi restaurant or a stylish Japanese bistro. Ginza Six basement food hall (B2F) is excellent for high-quality prepared foods and sweets.

meals.breakfast: Café in Ginza or hotel — ¥700–¥1,200
meals.lunch: Miraikan café or Odaiba food court — ¥1,000–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Ginza sushi or Japanese bistro — ¥2,500–¥4,000

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is closed on Tuesdays — Monday is a great day to visit. Book popular Ginza restaurants in advance for dinner. Ginza is walkable from Tsukiji (about 15 minutes).

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shibuya (渋谷). Visit the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing — watch the organized chaos from the Starbucks or Mag's Park overlook. Walk up to Shibuya Sky observation deck for aerial crossing views (¥2,000, book online).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shibuya's tech and youth culture scene — visit Shibuya 109 (fashion tech), Loft (lifestyle goods), and Tokyu Hands (now Hands) for innovative Japanese products and gadgets. Walk through the trendy Daikanyama and Nakameguro area along the canal.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Nakameguro — a hip neighborhood with excellent restaurants along the canal. Try a Japanese craft burger spot, a modern izakaya, or Korean-Japanese fusion. Return to hotel via Hibiya Line.

meals.breakfast: Shibuya café or convenience store morning set — ¥600–¥1,000
meals.lunch: Shibuya food floor (Hikarie or Scramble Square basement) — ¥1,200–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Nakameguro canal-side restaurant — ¥2,000–¥3,500

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya Sky tickets should be booked online in advance. Daikanyama and Nakameguro are best explored on foot — a 15-minute walk from Shibuya Station.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Harajuku (原宿). Visit Meiji Shrine (明治神宮) in the morning for a peaceful forested walk and traditional Shinto experience. Free entry to the shrine grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street for quirky youth fashion and crepes. Then head to Omotesando (表参道) for upscale architecture, boutique shops, and the Omotesando Hills complex. Visit the Prada or Louis Vuitton buildings for their architectural design.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Omotesando or nearby Aoyama — try a stylish Japanese restaurant or a high-quality ramen shop. Return to Tsukiji via Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku crepe or café near Meiji Shrine — ¥600–¥1,000
meals.lunch: Omotesando café or Harajuku restaurant — ¥1,200–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Aoyama or Omotesando restaurant — ¥2,000–¥3,500

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is most peaceful early morning. Harajuku is busiest on weekends — a Wednesday visit will be more relaxed. Takeshita Street opens around 11:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku (新宿). Start with the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck — free entry, open from 9:30 AM, with excellent city views including Mt. Fuji on clear days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's tech and electronics district around Yodobashi-Akiba Shinjuku. Visit Isetan department store for high-end Japanese food basement (depachika). Walk through the narrow alleys of Golden Gai and Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) to soak in old Tokyo atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — tiny yakitori stalls with grilled skewers and beer under the train tracks. Iconic, atmospheric, and affordable. Great for solo or group dining.

meals.breakfast: Shinjuku café or convenience store — ¥600–¥1,000
meals.lunch: Isetan depachika (basement food hall) bento or standing sushi bar — ¥1,200–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori stalls — ¥2,000–¥3,000 including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building North Tower is free and a great budget alternative to paid observation decks. Golden Gai bars are tiny (6–8 seats) and each has a unique theme — perfect for an evening drink after dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Yanaka (谷中) — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old neighborhoods. Walk through Yanaka Cemetery (beautiful in spring), browse the Yanaka Ginza shopping street with traditional craft shops, tofu sellers, and local snack stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ueno (上野). Visit the Tokyo National Museum (東京国立博物館) — Japan's largest museum with an incredible collection of samurai armor, ceramics, and historical artifacts. Entry ¥1,000. Stroll through Ueno Park.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Ueno or Akihabara (nearby). Try an eel (unaju) restaurant — Ueno is famous for eel dishes. Alternatively, explore Ameyoko Market street food stalls before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza street snacks — korokke (croquette), dagashi sweets, ¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Ueno Park area or museum café — ¥1,000–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Ueno eel restaurant (unaju) or Ameyoko street food — ¥2,000–¥3,500

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays. Ameyoko Market is lively and great for budget street food in the early evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Toyosu Market (豊洲市場) — the official wholesale fish market that replaced Tsukiji's inner market. Book a viewing tour in advance to watch the famous tuna auction (very limited spots, apply months ahead) or visit the observation areas freely. Located near your hotel area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the teamLab Planets in Toyosu (if not visited on Day 3) — an immersive digital art experience focused on water and botanical themes. Book tickets online. Afterward, explore the Toyosu area's modern urban development.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a high-quality sushi restaurant near Tsukiji — this is your neighborhood, so splurge a little. Try Sushi Zanmai (24-hour sushi chain with excellent value) or a local omakase counter for a special experience.

meals.breakfast: Toyosu Market area café or sushi breakfast — ¥1,500–¥2,500
meals.lunch: Toyosu shopping mall food court — ¥1,000–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area quality sushi restaurant — ¥3,000–¥5,000

day_by_day.notes: Toyosu tuna auctions require advance lottery registration — check the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market website. teamLab Planets tickets must be booked online well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kawagoe (川越), known as 'Little Edo' — a beautifully preserved Edo-period town about 1 hour from Tokyo by train (Tobu Tojo Line from Ikebukuro). Explore the historic Kurazukuri Street with traditional clay-walled warehouses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Kawagoe — visit the Kashiya Yokocho (Candy Alley) for traditional Japanese sweets, try sweet potato snacks (a local specialty), and visit the Kitain Temple. Return to Tokyo by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening near the hotel. Try a new restaurant in the Tsukiji or Ginza area. Visit a local sento (public bath) for an authentic Japanese relaxation experience — Tsukiji area has several nearby.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or early café before departure — ¥600–¥1,000
meals.lunch: Kawagoe local restaurant — unagi (eel) or soba — ¥1,200–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Tsukiji or Ginza neighborhood restaurant — ¥2,000–¥3,000

day_by_day.notes: Kawagoe is easily done as a half-day or full-day trip. Round-trip train fare is approximately ¥900–¥1,200. The town is walkable once you arrive. Weekends can be busy — arrive by 10:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Koenji (高円寺) — a vibrant neighborhood known for its indie music scene, vintage clothing shops, and local café culture. Explore the covered shopping arcades (shotengai) and vintage stores. Very authentic, non-touristy Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Shimokitazawa (下北沢) — Tokyo's bohemian hub with secondhand bookshops, vinyl record stores, independent theatres, and local cafés. Perfect for tech culture enthusiasts interested in Japan's indie creative scene. Easily reached by Keio Inokashira Line.
day_by_day.evening: Final special dinner — choose a restaurant that represents your trip highlights. Consider a teppanyaki restaurant, a kaiseki (multi-course Japanese) set meal, or a high-quality ramen experience. Return to hotel for packing.

meals.breakfast: Koenji local café — ¥700–¥1,200
meals.lunch: Shimokitazawa indie café or curry restaurant — ¥1,000–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner — teppanyaki or kaiseki — ¥4,000–¥7,000

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa is best explored slowly — allow 3–4 hours. Many vintage shops open around noon. This is a great day for souvenir shopping for unique, non-touristy items. Pack your bags tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo. Take one last walk through the Tsukiji Outer Market for breakfast — enjoy your favorite stalls one more time. Pick up any last-minute food souvenirs: dried seafood, wasabi, Japanese tea, or packaged snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time — if afternoon/evening departure, visit a nearby spot like the Hama-rikyu Gardens one last time or browse Ginza for final gift shopping. Head to the airport with ample time (allow 2–3 hours before departure). Return Suica/Pasmo card at the airport for a refund if desired.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 13 incredible days in Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — final sushi or tamagoyaki breakfast — ¥1,000–¥1,800
meals.lunch: Airport or final Tokyo meal depending on departure time — ¥1,200–¥2,000
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Narita Express (N'EX) takes about 60–90 minutes to Narita Airport. Limousine Bus is comfortable with luggage. Keep ¥3,000–¥5,000 yen cash for airport transport and any last expenses. Suica card refund available at airport JR service counters (¥220 handling fee deducted).

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from legendary vendors. Engage with local chefs and discover the heart of Tokyo's food culture in one of the world's most famous market districts.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Transfer from airport to Tsukiji boutique hotel via private luxury car service. Check-in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk around Tsukiji neighborhood. Stroll along the Sumida River waterfront promenade, explore the iconic Tsukiji Hongan-ji Temple, and browse the lively Tsukiji Outer Market stalls for a first taste of the area's vibrant food culture.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at Sushi Saito (or comparable omakase counter in Ginza, a short taxi ride away) — a world-class nigiri experience showcasing the finest Edo-mae sushi craftsmanship. Toast to the journey with a glass of premium sake.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: Light snack at Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh tamagoyaki roll and a matcha from a market stall vendor upon arrival
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi dinner at a Ginza or Tsukiji-area top-tier sushi counter (¥30,000–¥50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light to recover from jet lag. Confirm private airport transfer in advance. Ask the hotel concierge to make omakase reservations weeks ahead as top counters book quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — an immersive guided premium experience sampling fresh sushi, house-made tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, sea urchin, and artisan street snacks. Meet local vendors and learn the history of this legendary market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit teamLab Planets or teamLab Borderless (whichever is currently operating) in Toyosu/Odaiba — a world-renowned digital art and tech installation that perfectly blends Japanese innovation with sensory art. Book a VIP time slot in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ginza Six's top-floor restaurant enclave — choose from a curated selection of premium Japanese kaiseki or contemporary French-Japanese fusion dining with sweeping city views.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — request a traditional Japanese breakfast set (rice, miso soup, grilled fish, pickles) or a Western option
meals.lunch: Gourmet bites during the Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — fresh otoro sushi, uni, and seasonal skewers
meals.dinner: Kaiseki or French-Japanese fusion at Ginza Six rooftop restaurant (¥25,000–¥45,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Tsukiji Outer Market is most vibrant between 7:00–10:00 AM; start early. Book teamLab tickets well in advance — popular slots sell out weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Hamarikyu Gardens — a stunning Edo-period landscape garden adjacent to Tsukiji, offering cherry blossom (late sakura) or spring foliage scenery. Enjoy a traditional matcha tea ceremony in the teahouse situated over the tidal pond.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara Electric Town — Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics district. Visit multi-floor electronics megastores (Yodobashi Camera, Sofmap), explore retro gaming arcades, and browse cutting-edge gadgets, robotics kits, and rare tech collectibles.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium teppanyaki restaurant in Ginza or Marunouchi — watch a master chef craft A5 Wagyu beef, lobster, and seasonal vegetables on an iron griddle with theatrical precision.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby artisan coffee shop in Tsukiji
meals.lunch: Akihabara lunch at a high-end ramen specialist — try a premium black truffle or lobster bisque ramen at a curated shop in the area
meals.dinner: A5 Wagyu teppanyaki at Ginza Ukai-tei or equivalent (¥30,000–¥60,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens is a 5-minute walk from the hotel — perfect for an early morning stroll. In Akihabara, look for the Robot Restaurant experience or a private retro gaming lounge for a premium tech culture deep-dive.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic waterfront island. Visit the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan), home to ASIMO robots, interactive AI exhibits, and a life-size Gaia sphere display. A must-see for tech enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore DiverCity Tokyo Plaza and the iconic life-size Gundam statue. Visit SONY's showroom or Panasonic's innovation center for hands-on experiences with next-generation consumer technology. Stroll the Rainbow Bridge promenade for panoramic skyline views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city for dinner at a premium yakiniku (Japanese BBQ) restaurant — savor A5 Miyazaki or Kobe beef cuts grilled tableside, paired with aged sake or Japanese whisky.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Odaiba waterfront — dine at a stylish seafood restaurant inside DiverCity or a premium ramen bar overlooking Tokyo Bay
meals.dinner: A5 Wagyu yakiniku at Ginza Yakiniku Jumbo or Ushigoro Bambina (¥20,000–¥40,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Take the Yurikamome monorail to Odaiba for a scenic, futuristic transit experience. Miraikan requires timed entry tickets — book online in advance. Saturday can be crowded; arrive at Miraikan when it opens at 10:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the upscale Omotesando and Aoyama district — Tokyo's answer to Paris's Champs-Élysées. Admire the iconic architectural flagship stores (Prada by Herzog & de Meuron, Tod's by Toyo Ito) and browse luxury boutiques along the tree-lined boulevard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Nezu Museum in Aoyama — a world-class collection of Asian antiquities set within a beautifully landscaped traditional Japanese garden. Afterward, explore the hidden backstreets of Daikanyama, Tokyo's most refined neighborhood, for artisan coffee and boutique design shops.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a celebrated Japanese restaurant in Omotesando or Minami-Aoyama — consider a reservation at a Michelin-starred kaiseki establishment showcasing seasonal spring ingredients (bamboo shoots, cherry blossom, young ferns).

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Eggs 'n Things or a premium café in Omotesando
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Nezu Museum café, surrounded by the serene garden landscape
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred kaiseki in Aoyama (¥30,000–¥50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sunday in Omotesando is lively but manageable in the morning. The Nezu Museum garden is especially beautiful in spring. Daikanyama's Tsutaya Books complex is worth a visit for its design-forward concept.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Toyosu Fish Market — the world's largest wholesale seafood market. Witness the legendary tuna auction (advance lottery required months ahead), observe the inner workings of Japan's premium seafood supply chain, and gain insight into the culture behind Tokyo's sushi obsession.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Shiodome and the Panasonic Shiodome Museum or the Advertising Museum Tokyo (ADMT) — explore Japan's creative and technological innovation through design, media, and advertising history. Walk through the sleek Caretta Shiodome complex.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a sky bar — The Peninsula Tokyo Bar or Conrad Tokyo's Twenty Eight bar, offering sweeping views of Tokyo Bay and the city skyline. Follow with an intimate dinner at a premium soba kaiseki restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the Toyosu market tour (tours often begin at 5:30–6:00 AM)
meals.lunch: Post-market sushi breakfast/lunch at Sushi Dai or Daiwa Sushi in Toyosu — a legendary experience with the freshest fish in the world
meals.dinner: Premium soba kaiseki or contemporary Japanese at a Ginza or Shiodome fine dining venue (¥20,000–¥35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Toyosu tuna auction lottery must be entered months in advance via the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market website. If unavailable, the viewing deck still offers an impressive look at the market operations. Confirm booking early.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — a UNESCO World Heritage mountain shrine complex approximately 2 hours from Tokyo by Shinkansen and limited express train. Explore the ornate Tosho-gu Shrine, Rinnoji Temple, and the sacred Yomeimon Gate amid lush cedar forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko's Futarasan Shrine and the tranquil Shinkyo Sacred Bridge over the Daiya River. Stroll through the forested mountain paths for a serene contrast to Tokyo's urban energy.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo. Relaxed dinner near the hotel in Ginza — visit a premium tempura counter for a refined, intimate meal of seasonal ingredients fried in pure sesame oil with masterful precision.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Traditional yuba (tofu skin) cuisine lunch at a Nikko specialty restaurant — a local delicacy unique to the region
meals.dinner: Premium tempura omakase at Ginza Kondo or equivalent (¥20,000–¥35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Nikko Pass for unlimited train and bus travel in the Nikko area. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the mountain shrine paths. Spring foliage in Nikko is stunning in mid-to-late April.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanaka — one of Tokyo's last preserved Shitamachi (old town) neighborhoods. Wander through the historic cemetery, browse artisan craft shops along Yanaka Ginza shopping street, and visit century-old temples and traditional craft studios.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno — Japan's oldest and largest museum, housing an extraordinary collection of samurai armor, ancient ceramics, Buddhist sculpture, and ukiyo-e woodblock prints. Book a premium private guided tour for deeper context.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Ueno or Akihabara — try a premium sukiyaki restaurant, enjoying thinly sliced Wagyu beef cooked tableside in a sweet soy broth and dipped in raw egg.

meals.breakfast: Artisan coffee and fresh-baked pastry at a Yanaka neighborhood café
meals.lunch: Traditional Japanese set meal (teishoku) at a long-established Yanaka or Nezu restaurant — grilled fish, rice, miso, pickles
meals.dinner: Premium sukiyaki at Imahan or Zakuro in Ueno (¥20,000–¥35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot — allow 2–3 hours to wander freely. The Tokyo National Museum requires timed entry on weekends; Wednesday is typically less crowded. A private museum guide can be arranged through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mori Art Museum and Tokyo City View observation deck in Roppongi Hills — one of Tokyo's premier contemporary art institutions with rotating world-class exhibitions. Enjoy panoramic 360-degree views of the city from the 52nd floor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Roppongi's art triangle — visit the National Art Center Tokyo (a stunning Kisho Kurokawa-designed building) and the Suntory Museum of Art in Tokyo Midtown. Browse premium designer boutiques in Tokyo Midtown's curated retail floors.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a celebrated French-Japanese restaurant in Roppongi or Azabu — Tokyo's most internationally sophisticated dining enclave. Pair with a curated wine list featuring Burgundy or Champagne selections.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Stylish café lunch at the National Art Center Tokyo's Brasserie Paul Bocuse — a premium French dining experience within the museum itself
meals.dinner: French-Japanese haute cuisine at Azabu Yukimura, Quintessence, or equivalent Michelin-starred venue (¥35,000–¥60,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Mori Art Museum is open until 22:00 on most days — consider visiting the observation deck at dusk for spectacular golden hour and nighttime city views. Book dinner reservations at least 2–3 weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private workshop experience — arrange through the hotel concierge a hands-on session with a Tokyo artisan: options include a private sushi-making class with a master chef, a ramen broth crafting workshop, or a traditional Japanese knife-making demonstration in Kappabashi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kappabashi Kitchenware Street — the world's premier destination for professional culinary tools, ceramics, lacquerware, and the famous plastic food display models. Shop for premium Japanese knives, cast iron tetsubin kettles, and handcrafted tableware.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style splurge dinner at one of Tokyo's most exclusive addresses — consider Saito, Sushi Yoshitake, or L'Effervescence for an extraordinary multi-course meal representing the pinnacle of Japanese culinary artistry.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium ramen specialist near Kappabashi — try a high-end Jiro-style or wagyu bone broth ramen
meals.dinner: Ultra-premium omakase or multi-course tasting menu at a 3-Michelin-star Tokyo restaurant (¥50,000–¥80,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Private artisan workshops must be arranged well in advance — the hotel concierge can facilitate introductions. Kappabashi is a short taxi ride from Tsukiji. Friday evenings in Tokyo's top restaurants are extremely competitive for reservations — book 4–6 weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hakone — a scenic mountain resort town 90 minutes from Tokyo by Romancecar luxury express train. Visit the Hakone Open Air Museum, featuring world-class sculptures by Picasso, Rodin, and Henry Moore set against mountain scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the Hakone Ropeway for aerial views of Mt. Fuji (weather permitting) and the volcanic Owakudani sulfur vents. Cruise across Lake Ashi on a pirate-themed sightseeing boat for classic Fuji reflection views.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a luxury ryokan (traditional inn) in Hakone for an overnight stay — experience kaiseki multi-course dinner, private onsen (hot spring) baths, and sleeping on futons in a tatami room. Recommended: Gora Kadan, Hakone Ginyu, or The Hoshi.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure or onboard the Romancecar dining service
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Hakone Open Air Museum café or a nearby mountain restaurant featuring local Hakone tofu and seasonal vegetables
meals.dinner: Ryokan kaiseki dinner — a 10–14 course seasonal feast served in your private room (included in ryokan rate, typically ¥50,000–¥100,000 per person per night)

day_by_day.notes: Book the luxury ryokan overnight at least 4–6 weeks in advance — top properties sell out quickly, especially on weekends. Purchase the Hakone Free Pass for unlimited transport. Mt. Fuji visibility is weather-dependent; April offers reasonable odds.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at the Hakone ryokan and enjoy a private morning onsen soak overlooking the mountain forest. Savor a traditional Japanese breakfast in your tatami room — grilled fish, tofu, rice, pickles, and seasonal accompaniments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Tokyo via Romancecar. Spend the afternoon in Shinjuku — explore the iconic Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (spring flowers, manicured French and English gardens) before diving into the sensory overload of Kabukicho and the Golden Gai bar district.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium izakaya in Shinjuku — a sophisticated version of Japan's beloved pub dining culture, featuring seasonal small plates, premium sake flights, and Japanese whisky pairings in an intimate setting.

meals.breakfast: Ryokan traditional Japanese breakfast (included in ryokan stay)
meals.lunch: Casual lunch on the Romancecar or at a Shinjuku station premium food hall (depachika) — pick up artisan bento boxes, wagashi sweets, and premium snacks
meals.dinner: Premium izakaya omakase at Shinjuku's Tsunahachi or a curated sake-pairing izakaya (¥15,000–¥25,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen closes on Mondays — Sunday is ideal. The Golden Gai district (tiny atmospheric bars seating 5–8 people) is a unique Tokyo experience; explore multiple bars for drinks and conversation with locals and travelers alike.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — revisit the Tsukiji Outer Market for a nostalgic farewell breakfast of fresh sushi and tamagoyaki. Browse artisan food stalls for premium Japanese food souvenirs: aged soy sauce, wasabi, dashi packs, matcha, and artisan pickles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping in Ginza — visit Itoya (the world's most beautiful stationery store), Mikimoto Pearl, and the Ginza Six department store's basement food hall (depachika) for premium Japanese confections, wagashi, and gourmet gifts. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a Ginza counter restaurant — a final intimate omakase or premium shabu-shabu experience to close out the journey on a high note. Depart for the airport via private luxury car transfer.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market farewell feast — fresh otoro nigiri, grilled scallops, tamagoyaki, and matcha
meals.lunch: Ginza depachika premium bento or a light meal at a Ginza café
meals.dinner: Final omakase or shabu-shabu dinner at a top Ginza counter (¥25,000–¥45,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport transfer, check-in, and security. Narita Airport requires 90 minutes travel time from central Tokyo; Haneda Airport is closer at 30–45 minutes. Confirm private car transfer the evening before. Keep carry-on space for premium food souvenirs purchased at Tsukiji and Ginza.
